messages:
maria: Hi team — had to call an ambulance last night while at a conference. Hospital says ambulance is out-of-network and that they should have gotten authorization. This was an emergency and I couldn't wait. How do I file a claim and get retroactive preauth so it gets processed at in‑network rates? What docs do I need to send?

benefits-bot: [Auto] You can submit urgent claims here: https://benefits.redwood.example/claims — see the 'Emergency services' section. Insurer urgent claims phone: 1-800-555-EMER (Mon-Fri 8a-6p).

sam_people_ops: Sorry to hear that, maria. Quick checklist to get started:
1) Request an itemized bill + ambulance run sheet from the provider.
2) Ask the hospital for an attestation / ER triage note stating it was an emergency.
3) Submit claim + uploads via the portal (link above) and include all docs.
4) Call insurer urgent line and request 'retroactive authorization for emergency ambulance' — get a ticket number.
5) cc benefits@redwood.com so we can open an internal case and follow up.

tomas_benefits: Also ask the provider for NPI and any billing codes they have (ambulance codes often show as A0428 or similar). If the insurer denies for being out-of-network, you'll want to file an appeal attaching the EOB, clinical notes, and the run sheet. Typical appeal ETA 30-45 days, but we can request expedited review for emergencies. I can draft the appeal letter if you want.

jordan_finance: FYI for reimbursement: Finance needs a PDF invoice (itemized), proof of payment (if you paid), and any claim number if the hospital bills you. If hospital bills the insurer directly, share the claim ID. Ping me when you submit and I'll note it for expense purposes.

maria: Thanks — hospital already gave an itemized bill + the run sheet. I don't see CPT codes, just 'ambulance service' line and a charge amount. Uploading now.

sam_people_ops: Paste the portal upload link / insurer ticket here once you have them. Quick email template you can send to insurer (copy/paste):

benefits-email:
```
To: claims@insurer.example
Subject: Urgent - Retroactive Auth Request for Emergency Ambulance - [Member: Maria Lopez, DOB: 1990-05-12]

Hi,
I received emergency ambulance transport on 03/15/2025. This was an emergency and required immediate transport. Per plan language for emergency services, we request retroactive authorization so services are processed at in‑network benefit levels. Attached: itemized bill, ambulance run sheet, ER triage note, proof of payment.

Please confirm receipt and provide next steps; we request expedited review.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Member ID: XXXXX
```

benefits-bot: Portal upload page: https://benefits.redwood.example/claims/upload — use priority code EMERG for faster intake (code valid for 7 days).

maria: Done — uploaded docs and called insurer, they gave ticket #987654. Link: https://benefits.redwood.example/claims/view/987654 (I also cc'd benefits@redwood.com).

sam_people_ops: Got it — we're opening an internal case and will follow up with the insurer if there's no response in 5 business days. If they deny, we'll escalate to Tomás to prepare the appeal packet.

tomas_benefits: I'll take it if needed. Maria — save screenshots of ER timestamps, discharge papers, or any 911/dispatch confirmation if you have them; that strengthens the emergency argument.

maria: Will do. Really appreciate the quick help — thanks everyone :heart:
